crisis.label: High
crisis.detail: Aug 7: Reuters reports Hormuz traffic dwindled to 33 vessels from Monday to Thursday versus 50 in the week-ago period; only four transited Thursday, including one VLCC, while six crude tankers exited and 21 vessels entered, mostly via the Iranian route (Reuters/Kpler, Aug 7). A proposed Iran-Oman passage framework faces U.S. sanctions and restrictive insurance clauses (Reuters, Aug 6), and an Iranian parliamentary committee is reviewing a draft bill to bar U.S., Israeli and other hostile vessels, with fines up to 20% of cargo value (Reuters, Aug 6). No signed reopening is confirmed. Brent is $83.46, WTI $78.32 and TTF 55.51 EUR/MWh on Aug 7. Crisis level remains 4 (High); stress raised to 55% while base falls to 15%.

todaysEvents.summary: Hormuz traffic falls to four vessels
todaysEvents.delta: Up: Reuters reports four vessels transited on Aug 6, including one VLCC, two LPG carriers and one minor bulk carrier; only six crude tankers exited this week and 21 vessels entered, mostly via the Iranian route. Source: Reuters/Kpler, Aug 7.

todaysEvents.summary: Iran draft bill targets hostile ships
todaysEvents.delta: Up: An Iranian parliamentary committee is reviewing a preliminary bill that would bar U.S., Israeli and other hostile vessels from Hormuz and fine violations up to 20% of cargo value; the draft remains under expert review. Source: Reuters, Aug 6.

Up: A proposed Iran-Oman framework would give Tehran control over inbound traffic and route clearance, but four industry sources told Reuters that U.S. sanctions and restrictive insurance clauses make fees and payments difficult for shippers. No reopening is signed. Source: Reuters, Aug 6.

scenarios.label: Base
scenarios.description: A signed Iran-Oman framework restores non-discriminatory, fee-free transit and traffic rebuilds gradually; the current proposal remains unsigned and faces sanctions and insurance barriers (Reuters, Aug 6). Brent moves toward $75-85 as the risk premium eases, while Qatar's force majeure still limits LNG availability.

scenarios.label: Stress
scenarios.description: No workable agreement emerges: Iran retains conditional control over routing, draft restrictions deter U.S. and Israeli-linked shipping, and traffic stays depressed at 33 vessels Monday-Thursday versus 50 in the prior week, with only four on Aug 6 (Reuters/Kpler, Aug 7). Brent holds $78-95 and JKM stays elevated on Qatar force majeure through mid-September.

scenarios.label: Tail
scenarios.description: The draft restrictions harden into exclusion, fees or attacks widen and the Iran-Oman channel fails, driving a renewed closure of Hormuz and spillover into the Red Sea. Brent returns to $105-135+/bbl and JKM moves above $30/MMBtu as Gulf cargoes become inaccessible.

traceInputs.headline: Reuters (Aug 7) reports Hormuz traffic at 33 vessels from Monday to Thursday versus 50 in the prior-week period; four transited Aug 6, including one VLCC, two LPG carriers and one minor bulk carrier. Six crude tankers exited and 21 vessels entered, mostly via the Iranian route, with no new fixtures. Reuters (Aug 6) says the proposed Iran-Oman passage framework faces U.S. sanctions and restrictive insurance clauses, while a draft bill may bar U.S., Israeli and other hostile vessels. Windward's Aug 2 review records a second confirmed Qatari LNG cargo strike on July 31. Qatar force majeure remains carried through mid-September, current route-normalised freight and war-risk costs remain unavailable, and no signed reopening is confirmed.

priceNarratives.Brent: Pre-shock ~$65 -> $126 wartime high intraday (Day 59, Apr 30, CNBC/CNN) -> $98.57 (Jun 3 D93 peak) -> $90.12 (Aug 1, Yahoo Finance BZ=F) as tanker incidents and Kuwait attacks kept risk elevated -> $83.61 (Aug 3, -4.9%, Investing.com) as Trump canceled planned strikes -> $78.88 (Aug 4 close, -5.8%, Trading Economics) as reopening hopes grew -> $79.18 (Aug 5, -0.2%, Trading Economics) -> $83.46 (Aug 7, Yahoo Finance BZ=F, -0.37%) as Reuters reported 33 Hormuz vessels Monday-Thursday versus 50 in the prior week and a proposed Iran-Oman passage framework faced sanctions and insurance barriers. Working range $75-85 base (signed workable deal); $78-95 stress (conditional routing); $105-135+ tail (renewed closure).
priceNarratives.JKM LNG: Baseline $9.5 -> $23.40/MMBtu (Day 20, Reuters/Platts) -> $19.93/MMBtu (Jul 16, Trading Economics) -> $22.00/MMBtu (Jul 24, Reuters September-delivery assessment) as sustained Hormuz disruption tightened Asian LNG balances; carried at $22.00 pending a newer weekly assessment. Contextual CFD reference $21.14/MMBtu (Trading Economics, Aug 6, +1.08%). Qatar force majeure is carried through mid-September from the Reuters Jul 23 notice; the reported mid-October extension remains unconfirmed.

The marker remains elevated versus the pre-crisis baseline while Qatar LNG force majeure and constrained Hormuz traffic persist.
